result.title: Teacher-Guided Multimodal Dual Representation Reconstruction for Egocentric Human Activity Recognition
result.summary: Multimodal Egocentric Human Activity Recognition (Ego-HAR) leverages complementary cues from first-person vision (V) and inertial sensor data (S) to recognize daily activities, where video mainly captures appearance and object-related context while inertial signals capture motion cues that video may miss. However, existing pre-training methods typically supervise the fused representation with a single joint objective, which may underemphasize the complementarity between the two modalities and limit the model's ability to learn from distinct modality-oriented signals. To address this issue, we propose Multimodal Dual Representation Reconstruction (MDR2), a teacher-guided pre-training framework in which frozen, label-informed video and inertial teachers each provide dense, modality-specific targets to a multimodal student trained on temporally sparse inputs. On the EvIs-Kitchen dataset, MDR2 improves noun/verb F1-macro over the supervised M-Baseline by 9.20/6.17 points at K=4 video key frames and by 1.21/1.82 points at K=32. These results show that MDR2 consistently achieves higher mean recognition performance across the evaluated video-observation settings under the unified backbone setting, with more pronounced gains under sparse inputs.

AI.brief_summary: 该文面向第一视角人体活动识别，提出教师引导的多模态双表征重构预训练框架：用冻结的、可见标签的视频教师与惯性教师分别向多模态学生提供密集的模态专属目标，学生在时间稀疏输入上训练，稀疏视频帧下收益更明显。
AI.relevance_reason: 其用模态专属教师目标替代单一融合监督，可能为 LVR 中融合表征如何保留视觉与运动等互补信息、避免信息坍缩提供可核查的监督设计线索，但论文本身不涉及推理期 latent 状态生成。
